title: Deceleration and Re‑Entry Playbook: Sabbaticals, Parental Leave, and Extended Absences
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard process for supporting employees who take extended leaves (sabbaticals, parental leave, medical leave >8 weeks) and for their structured re‑entry. The goal is to preserve psychological safety and career trajectory while maintaining team continuity and measurable ramp-up to full productivity. This is a people-ops + manager playbook, intended for managers, HR business partners, people-ops leads, and SRE/product partners who must coordinate coverage and knowledge transfer.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees and long-term contractors with approved leaves of 8+ weeks.
- Covers pre-leave deceleration, formal handoff, coverage plans, re-entry options (full-time, phased, part-time), 30/60/90 re-onboarding, promotion/compensation considerations, and measurement.
- Does NOT replace legal leave entitlement or benefits policies; see Payroll & Leaves policy for statutory specifics.

Principles:
- Respect autonomy: Encourage employee-driven leave plans and voluntary check-in cadence.
- Career neutrality: Time on leave should not be a de facto blocker for promotion or role changes; managers must document rationale for any adverse decisions.
- Predictable coverage: Teams must plan a coverage path with named owners and success criteria.
- Measured ramp: Define concrete metrics that signal readiness to be considered ‘fully productive’.

High-level timeline (recommended):
1) Pre-Leave (8–4 weeks before): Deceleration and documentation phase.
   - Employee + manager agree on public leave dates, expected return window, and preferred communication.
   - Create Handoff Plan (see template below).
   - Identify interim owner(s) and prepare temporary access/role changes.
2) Pre-Leave (4–0 weeks): Freeze and transition.
   - Code freeze for major changes tied to feature slates if feasible.
   - Execute knowledge-transfer sessions (recorded).
   - Confirm payroll/benefits and HR checklists complete.
3) Leave period: Minimal required check-ins (employee preference drives cadence).
4) Return (0–2 weeks): Administrative re-onboarding.
   - Restore access, reintroduce to team, set re-entry 30/60/90 plan.
5) Re-Entry Ramp (weeks 1–12): Measured skill/capacity recovery with staged ownership.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Manager:
  - Initiate leave planning conversation and file Handoff Plan.
  - Nominate interim owners and set rolling goals.
  - Own performance calibration implications and document decisions.
- Employee on leave:
  - Provide prioritized list of active projects, single-line definitions, and contact preferences.
  - Record 2–3 short ‘how-to’ videos for key workflows when possible.
- Interim Owner(s):
  - Maintain the listed SLOs, keep stakeholder updates, and escalate unresolved issues.
- People-ops (HRBP):
  - Validate legal/benefits steps, advise on re-entry options, and ensure equity checks.
- Tech Ops / SRE / Security:
  - Manage temporary access changes and audit logging.

Handoff Plan (must be created pre-leave):
- Document title: Handoff — [Employee] — [Primary projects]
- Top-line summary (1 paragraph)
- Active tickets and their owners (link to ticket list)
- Pending PRs and blockers (include approximate effort estimate)
- Release windows and rollback plans (if applicable)
- Decision log: recent trade-offs and rationale (2–5 bullets)
- Who to contact for escalation and their communication channel
- Known risks and mitigation steps

Coverage options (choose one and document rationale):
- Short-term shift: redistribute tasks across existing team members (low cost, high distributed risk).
- Interim IC hire (contractor) for critical path work (preferred when specialized knowledge is required).
- Temporary backfill (headcount reallocation for leaves > 6 months).

Administrative steps checklist (manager + HR):
- [ ] Submit Leave Request in Workday or internal portal
- [ ] Handoff Plan filed in team space and linked to calendar
- [ ] Define interim owner(s) and permissions
- [ ] Schedule recorded knowledge-transfer sessions
- [ ] Update oncall rota and runbooks (SRE)
- [ ] Confirm benefits/payroll entries
- [ ] Schedule re-entry meeting 2–4 weeks before return (employee preference)

Re-Entry options (employee choice; manager + HR to support):
- Full-time immediate return (standard)
- Phased return (recommended default for medical/parental leaves): 2–8 weeks of reduced hours with a documented ramp plan
- Part-time for an agreed window (documented impact to compensation/benefits where applicable)

30/60/90 Re-Entry Plan template (manager + employee co-authored):
- 30 days (intended outcomes): reconnect to codebase, close 1 small ticket, attend core syncs, pair with two teammates. Success signals: unblock time <48h for core repo, two integration PRs merged.
- 60 days (intended outcomes): re-assume ownership for a medium-priority subcomponent, lead one demo. Success signals: owner signoff, automated tests passing, stakeholder acceptance.
- 90 days (intended outcomes): full role responsibilities restored (unless a longer phased plan agreed). Success signals: measurable baseline metrics tied to pre-leave performance or documented adjusted goals.

Promotion and compensation guidance:
- Default: time on approved leave is not punitive. If promotion cycles occur during leave, managers must:
  1) Proactively evaluate evidence available (pre-leave work, handoff artifacts, return ramp progress).
  2) If insufficient evidence exists, document a clear path and timeline to collect evaluation evidence post-return (e.g., 6–12 weeks of performance).
  3) Any exceptions must be routed to people-ops/compensation for review.

Performance management and feedback cadence post-return:
- Weekly 1:1s for first 8 weeks focused on reorientation and well-being.
- Monthly milestone review against 30/60/90 plan up to 6 months.
- Explicitly document any performance concerns and remediation timeline; managers should avoid surprises by initiating early feedback sessions.

Measurement and signals of successful re-entry:
- Time-to-first-merge (target: within 14 business days)
- Number of restored primary responsibilities (target: 80% by day 90)
- Manager-reported confidence score (weekly, 1–5 scale)
- Employee-reported readiness and well-being check (pulse at weeks 2, 6, 12)

Equity & exceptions:
- People-ops will run quarterly audits comparing promotion/payout outcomes for employees who took leaves vs. similar peers.
- Any perceived negative impact should trigger a case review with the HRBP and manager.

Security and access notes:
- Access suspension should be minimal and reversible. Use documented groups and temporary tokens.
- SRE must record all access changes in the access audit log; manager must confirm access restoration on day 0 of return.

Sample communications (templates):
- All-hands leave announcement (short):
  "[Name] will be on leave from [start] to [end]. During this period, [Interim Owner] will own [projects]. Please route urgent issues to [email/contact]. Join us in wishing them well."

- Re-entry welcome note (team message):
  "Welcome back [Name]! We'll do a light re-onboarding schedule: 1:1 at 10am, team sync at 2pm, and a reorientation doc linked here. Reach out if you need adjustments to your schedule."

Knowledge transfer artifacts (recommended):
- 2–4 short screen-capture videos (5–10 min) for high-value workflows
- A README that answers: What it is, Where to look, Who to call (top three people), Quick triage steps
- Tag important PRs with label "reentry-reference"

Conflict scenarios and escalation path:
- If interim owner disagrees on priority, escalate to manager -> product lead -> people-ops.
- If manager and employee disagree on phased return terms, HRBP mediates and documents final agreement.

Related pages and templates (links):
- Internal: Payroll & Leaves policy (link)
- Internal: Manager Performance Calibration playbook (link)
- Template: Handoff Plan (link)
- Template: Re-entry 30/60/90 (link)

Appendix A — Example Handoff checklist (text table):
- Column headers: Item | Owner | Status | Notes
- Example row: "Feature X integration" | "Nina Patel (interim)" | "In progress" | "API contract stable; tests flake on staging"

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions:
Q: Can employees be contacted during leave?
A: Contact frequency is employee preference; only urgent safety or legal matters may warrant outreach. Document preferred method in the Handoff Plan.

Q: Who signs off on ending phased return early?
A: The manager and employee mutually agree; people-ops should be informed and the decision recorded in the performance notes.
